mathematics: Tower orientation is fine Z to coarse U: href states equality of Z implies equality of U, and history_refinement_factors gives U=g∘Z.
On each positive Z atom, an actual representative exists. On a good atom, hpoint bounds E and event inclusion bounds E∧S by E on the same atom. No conditioning on S is introduced.
On a false-good representative, hS propagates false S to every member of that fine atom; numerator for E∧S is exactly zero and hb yields the bound.
Finite coarse-atom averaging uses normalized nonnegative conditional weights and positive coarse hu.
statement_model: hS explicitly supplies fine-history measurability; it does not require coarse-history measurability.
hpoint required only at positive-mass fine atoms whose representative is good.
E itself need not be fine-history measurable.
S remains inside E∧S in conclusion; statement does not incorrectly assert P(E|U)≤b or P(E|U,S)≤b.
adversarial: Null fine atoms are excluded from hpoint and carry zero conditional tower weight.
Fine atoms with S false do not invoke hpoint and contribute zero.
Negative b is prohibited by hb, necessary for bad-only fibers.
Empty/unattained values of Z use arbitrary factor-map default u, irrelevant on actual support.
Positive coarse fiber required; no normalization of null coarse history is asserted.
